  },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"paragraph\",\n      \"data\": {\n        \"text\": \"Beyond that optimism garnered by that youthful Danielson-Brandsegg-Nygard combination for the game winner and the 4\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"paragraph\",\n      \"data\": {\n        \"text\": \"At this stage of the (pre-)season, Ville Husso's biggest priority is re-gaining the trust of the Red Wings' coaching staff.  With his performance Tuesday, he did strong work toward that end, as he was the unambiguous standout in an altogether strong Detroit performance.\u003cbr>\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"image\",\n      \"data\": {\n        \"file\": {\n          \"url\": \"https://thehockeynews.com/.image/c_fit,h_600,w_600/MjA5NDQ3NTM3NjM4MTIzMTU4/usatsi_22037514.jpg\"\n        },\n        \"caption\": \"Dec 2, 2023; Montreal, Quebec, CAN; Detroit Red Wings goalie Ville Husso (35) looks on during warm-up before the game against the Montreal Canadiens at Bell Centre.\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"paragraph\",\n      \"data\": {\n        \"text\": \"Husso opened with a perfect 14 saves on 14 shots in the first period.  He conceded early in the second, but that came only after a strong save in tight, before Rickard Rakell was able to bury a rebound.  He would ultimately punctuate his night with a number of strong stops on high-danger Penguin looks in the third period, including a desperate net-front scramble with a minute to play.  Perhaps most important of all for Husso is that he went a full 60 minutes healthy, consistent, and stingy.  \"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"paragraph\",\n      \"data\": {\n        \"text\": \"By night's end, he made an outstanding 43 saves on 44 shots, against a Pittsburgh lineup that featured its fair share of prospective AHLers but also Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin, and Kris Letang.  As ever, the \\\"it's only pre-season\\\" caveat applies, but it would be hard to ask for a stronger or more encouraging performance from Husso as the regular season beckons.\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"header\",\n      \"data\": {\n        \"text\": \"Lombardi Scores, Grinds\",\n        \"level\": 4\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"paragraph\",\n      \"data\": {\n        \"text\": \"Amadeus Lombardi had a strong performance for Detroit.  The highlight was a goal, scored after an assertive cut inside, then ripped shot past Tristan Jarry.  In a pre-season defined by talent and experience disparities, it's worth noting Jarry's status as an established NHL netminder.  There's no doubting Lombardi's speed or stick-handling, but there is some question as to his abilities to deploy those skills in the NHL.  This goal is a great example of what you'd like to see even more of from Lombardi: driving offense into the slot for high-danger chances.  If he can make a habit of that, he can surely contribute at the NHL level.\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"text\": \"The Red Wings shuffled lines somewhat liberally Tuesday night, but a few shifts saw Lombardi alongside Elmer Soderblom and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard.  It was nice to see that trio apply some forechecking pressure together, even if it didn't yield a goal.  That's right up Brandsegg-Nygard's alley, but it's another area where Soderblom and Lombardi have room for growth.  None of that trio has an especially realistic place at an NHL roster spot for the time being, but if Brandsegg-Nygard opts to stick around North America, it could be a fun line for the Griffins this year in Grand Rapids.\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"header\",\n      \"data\": {\n        \"text\": \"Motte-Veleno-Watson Previews Re-Defined Fourth Line\",\n        \"level\": 4\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"paragraph\",\n      \"data\": {\n        \"text\": \"In the Tyler Motte, Joe Veleno, and Austin Watson triumvirate, coach Derek Lalonde offered a decently realistic preview of the Red Wings fourth line come October 10th.  Veleno would be the sole holdover from last year's fourth line, but the introduction of the industrious, tight checking Motte and simple, physical Watson represents a clear change of direction from last year's fourth line mainstays Robby Fabbri and Daniel Sprong.\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"paragraph\",\n      \"data\": {\n        \"text\": \"I wrote this afternoon about \u003ca href=\\\"https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/detroit-red-wings/game-day/where-does-veleno-fit-in-for-the-red-wings\\\">potential trajectories for Joe Veleno\u003c/a> to become an essential piece of the Red Wings plan moving forward, and one of those paths is by becoming a specialized defensive fourth line center.  He's spent time in that role, but playing with the likes of Motte and Watson would represent a pivot toward a different version of it and perhaps a more sustainable one.  Meanwhile, as the Red Wings look to tighten defensively, the fourth line seems an obvious area in which to emphasize that message, so that construction feels consistent with the stated path toward improved results.\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"paragraph\",\n      \"data\": {\n        \"text\": \"That success, of course, raises the question of Watson and his PTO.  Strictly speaking, there isn't a roster spot for him, but...perhaps one class="paragraph-tool undefined"><div class="ce-paragraph cdx-block"><p>Husso opened with a perfect 14 saves on 14 shots in the first period.  He conceded early in the second, but that came only after a strong save in tight, before Rickard Rakell was able to bury a rebound.  He would ultimately punctuate his night with a number of strong stops on high-danger Penguin looks in the third period, including a desperate net-front scramble with a minute to play.  Perhaps most important of all for Husso is that he went a full 60 minutes healthy, consistent, and stingy.  </p></div></div></div></div><div class="lg:hidden"><div class=""></div></div><div class="ce-block"><div class="ce-block__content"><div class="paragraph-tool undefined"><div class="ce-paragraph cdx-block"><p>By night's end, he made an outstanding 43 saves on 44 shots, against a Pittsburgh lineup that featured its fair share of prospective AHLers but also Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin, and Kris Letang.  As ever, the "it's only pre-season" caveat applies, but it would be hard to ask for a stronger or more encouraging performance from Husso as the regular season beckons.</p></div></div></div></div><div class="ce-block"><div class="ce-block__content"><div class="header-tool undefined"><span class="leading-tight text-ellipsis overflow-hidden whitespace-normal class="paragraph-tool undefined"><div class="ce-paragraph cdx-block"><p>Amadeus Lombardi had a strong performance for Detroit.  The highlight was a goal, scored after an assertive cut inside, then ripped shot past Tristan Jarry.  In a pre-season defined by talent and experience disparities, it's worth noting Jarry's status as an established NHL netminder.  There's no doubting Lombardi's speed or stick-handling, but there is some question as to his abilities to deploy those skills in the NHL.  This goal is a great example of what you'd like to see even more of from Lombardi: driving offense into the slot for high-danger chances.  If he can make a habit of that, he can surely contribute at the NHL level.</p></div></div></div></div><div class="transition cursor-pointer flex justify-center some forechecking pressure together, even if it didn't yield a goal.  That's right up Brandsegg-Nygard's alley, but it's another area where Soderblom and Lombardi have room for growth.  None of that trio has an especially realistic place at an NHL roster spot for the time being, but if Brandsegg-Nygard opts to stick around North America, it could be a fun line for the Griffins this year in Grand class="ce-block__content"><div class="paragraph-tool undefined"><div class="ce-paragraph cdx-block"><p>In the Tyler Motte, Joe Veleno, and Austin Watson triumvirate, coach Derek Lalonde offered a decently realistic preview of the Red Wings fourth line come October 10th.  Veleno would be the sole holdover from last year's fourth line, but the introduction of the industrious, tight checking Motte and simple, physical Watson represents a clear change of direction from last year's fourth line mainstays Robby Fabbri and Daniel Sprong.</p></div></div></div></div><div class="ce-block"><div class="ce-block__content"><div class="paragraph-tool undefined"><div class="ce-paragraph cdx-block"><p>I wrote this afternoon about <a href="https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/detroit-red-wings/game-day/where-does-veleno-fit-in-for-the-red-wings">potential trajectories for Joe Veleno</a> to become an essential piece of the Red Wings plan moving forward, and one of those paths is by becoming a specialized defensive fourth line center.  He's spent time in that role, but playing with the likes of Motte and Watson would represent a pivot toward a different version of it and perhaps a more sustainable one.  Meanwhile, as the Red Wings look to tighten defensively, the fourth line seems an obvious area in which to emphasize that message, so that construction feels consistent with the stated path toward improved results.</p></div></div></div></div><div class="transition cursor-pointer flex justify-center items-center w-max h-max NHL\n\nTuesday night in Pittsburgh, the Red Wings scored a 2-1 victory over the host\nPenguins on the strength of a late winner from 2023 first round draft pick Nate\nDanielson.  Danieslon took advantage of a transition opportunity to drive the\nnet and convert for the game-winner off an assist from 2024's first rounder,\nMichael Brandsegg-Nygard:\n\n\n\nBeyond that optimism garnered by that youthful Danielson-Brandsegg-Nygard\ncombination for the game winner and the result itself, here are three notes from\nDetroit's performance:\n\nHUSSO IMPRESSES\n\nAt this stage of the (pre-)season, Ville Husso's biggest priority is re-gaining\nthe trust of the Red Wings' coaching staff.  With his performance Tuesday, he\ndid strong work toward that end, as he was the unambiguous standout in an\naltogether strong Detroit performance.\n\n\nDec 2, 2023; Montreal, Quebec, CAN; Detroit Red Wings goalie Ville Husso (35)\nlooks on during warm-up before the game against the Montreal Canadiens at Bell\nCentre.\n[https://thehockeynews.com/.image/c_fit,h_600,w_600/MjA5NDQ3NTM3NjM4MTIzMTU4/usatsi_22037514.jpg]\nDec 2, 2023; Montreal, Quebec, CAN; Detroit Red Wings goalie Ville Husso (35)\nlooks on during warm-up before the game against the Montreal Canadiens at Bell\nCentre.\n\nHusso opened with a perfect 14 saves on 14 shots in the first period.  He\nconceded early in the second, but that came only after a strong save in tight,\nbefore Rickard Rakell was able to bury a rebound.  He would ultimately punctuate\nhis night with a number of strong stops on high-danger Penguin looks in the\nthird period, including a desperate net-front scramble with a minute to play. \nPerhaps most important of all for Husso is that he went a full 60 minutes\nhealthy, consistent, and stingy.  \n\nBy night's end, he made an outstanding 43 saves on 44 shots, against a\nPittsburgh lineup that featured its fair share of prospective AHLers but also\nSidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin, and Kris Letang.  As ever, the \"it's only\npre-season\" caveat applies, but it would be hard to ask for a stronger or more\nencouraging performance from Husso as the regular season beckons.\n\nLOMBARDI SCORES, GRINDS\n\nAmadeus Lombardi had a strong performance for Detroit.  The highlight was a\ngoal, scored after an assertive cut inside, then ripped shot past Tristan\nJarry.  In a pre-season defined by talent and experience disparities, it's worth\nnoting Jarry's status as an established NHL netminder.  There's no doubting\nLombardi's speed or stick-handling, but there is some question as to his\nabilities to deploy those skills in the NHL.  This goal is a great example of\nwhat you'd like to see even more of from Lombardi: driving offense into the slot\nfor high-danger chances.  If he can make a habit of that, he can surely\ncontribute at the NHL level.\n\n\n\nThe Red Wings shuffled lines somewhat liberally Tuesday night, but a few shifts\nsaw Lombardi alongside Elmer Soderblom and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard.  It was\nnice to see that trio apply some forechecking pressure together, even if it\ndidn't yield a goal.  That's right up Brandsegg-Nygard's alley, but it's another\narea where Soderblom and Lombardi have room for growth.  None of that trio has\nan especially realistic place at an NHL roster spot for the time being, but if\nBrandsegg-Nygard opts to stick around North America, it could be a fun line for\nthe Griffins this year in Grand Rapids.\n\nMOTTE-VELENO-WATSON PREVIEWS RE-DEFINED FOURTH LINE\n\nIn the Tyler Motte, Joe Veleno, and Austin Watson triumvirate, coach Derek\nLalonde offered a decently realistic preview of the Red Wings fourth line come\nOctober 10th.  Veleno would be the sole holdover from last year's fourth line,\nbut the introduction of the industrious, tight checking Motte and simple,\nphysical Watson represents a clear change of direction from last year's fourth\nline mainstays Robby Fabbri and Daniel Sprong.\n\nI wrote this afternoon about potential trajectories for Joe Veleno\n[https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/detroit-red-wings/game-day/where-does-veleno-fit-in-for-the-red-wings]\nto become an essential piece of the Red Wings plan moving forward, and one of\nthose paths is by becoming a specialized defensive fourth line center.  He's\nspent time in that role, but playing with the likes of Motte and Watson would\nrepresent a
